e54316070821e5b2a17d63a075b09d8e59783742: A resort on a human scale, Glacier du Pitztal focuses on warm welcomes and proximity rather than impressive figures. Its 41 km of runs are ideal for a 3 to 4 day stay, especially for families or skiers who don't need to constantly change their playground. Glacier du Pitztal's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for learning to ski with children. As for snow, Glacier du Pitztal is in a strong position with its summit at 3440 m: even in capricious winters, the upper runs hold up well until April. The village at 2685 m is also well placed to offer comfortable conditions from mid-December. The budget for a stay at Glacier du Pitztal is clearly high: €77 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and high-altitude restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Glacier du Pitztal does not rival the giants of skiing, and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

e55432758ebe1be4265d39df527ab6cd9745e2d3: Praz-sur-Arly offers 90 km of well-marked runs — a mid-sized ski area that's ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 36 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in peak season. Praz-sur-Arly's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It's one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for getting children started on skiing. Praz-sur-Arly's altitude (1036 m at the bottom, 2070 m at the top) helps it maintain decent snow cover in midwinter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it's worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. The day lift pass at €41 places Praz-sur-Arly in the intermediate bracket for budget — neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short: Praz-sur-Arly is one of those rare resorts that combines a genuine village, a sincerely family-friendly atmosphere and runs suited to everyone. It's hard to have a bad stay here.

e5b5f6693ff0742b0bcb57ecf050a75fef446660: The Méribel ski area, with its 150 km of runs, offers something for every type of skier: large enough not to go round in circles for a week, yet compact enough to find your favourite sectors again easily. The 39 lifts let you link descents without long queues. Méribel's DNA is high end: the accommodation, mountain restaurants and resort services reflect a clientele that doesn't count the cost. With a day pass at 69€, the stay has a price, but the experience lives up to it for anyone who wants to indulge without compromise. With a summit at 2952 m and a village at 1450 m, snow cover in Méribel is generally reliable from January to late March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause tension early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly once serious snowfalls arrive. The budget for a stay in Méribel is clearly high: 69€ for the day pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but be aware of it before you go. In short: Méribel isn't for everyone, but for those who can afford it, it's probably one of the best skiing experiences in Europe.
